_about: The story's words. The indictment is read one count per death, in order; after the last count, a death adds one of the addenda. {years}, {total} and {year} are filled in by the core. death_titles head the indictment by the zone you died in. interludes are read between a zone's boss and the next zone, by the zone just left. The verdict follows the last built zone's boss (the Idiot God, sung to sleep); its last line is mechanical and says what the build holds. A boss's bars, when it has them, name each phase's bar on the HUD; the last is the lullaby's. mission: the last mission's words, opened by putting the Idiot God to sleep: its brief (read before it begins), its interludes by the zone just left (the fourth's is where reality breaks, and you wake at home), and its ending (the verdict after Chumbles is fed).
case: TRIBUNAL OF THE LAST HOUR | CASE 2081-1 | THE CITY OF MERIDIAN v. THE DEFENDANT
sentencing: On March 14, 2081, every clock in Meridian stopped at 9:14 p.m. Nine million people were trapped in the same evening. The Tribunal says you caused it.
You were found guilty of the Stilling. You remember none of the trial. Your sentence is Corrective Return: go back to that night, reach the Observatory, and stop your older self.
The Bailiff of Hours was ordered to deliver you to 2081. It has never missed its mark before.

Fifty years early. The Tribunal calls it an error. The Bailiff says it followed its orders. The court will read your charges each time you die. Your task has not changed: reach 2081 and stop your older self.
counts: COUNT 01 | ACCESS. On March 14, 2081, you entered the Meridian Observatory with a key issued years earlier to another keeper.
COUNT 02 | THE DEVICE. Inside, you activated the Long Door. You had spent eleven years building it. Its official records called it a weather clock.
COUNT 03 | INTENT. The Long Door was built to hold one evening in place, so that one person would never have to leave it. You knew something else could pass through.
COUNT 04 | THE STILLING. At 9:14 p.m., the clocks stopped across Meridian. Nine million people lost the next morning. Your notes called it a small adjustment.
COUNT 05 | THE VICTIMS. The people of Meridian remain inside that evening. They cannot move on. The court has found no way to reach them.
COUNT 06 | THE PERSON. Among them is the person you meant to keep. They are in a kitchen, mid-sentence, unaware that the world has stopped.
COUNT 07 | AFTERMATH. You walked through the silent city for thirty-one days. No one saw you. No one could.
COUNT 08 | TESTIMONY. You surrendered to the Tribunal, refused counsel, and gave one statement: I would do it again.
COUNT 09 | JUDGMENT. The court treats that statement as proof you remain a threat. It orders your return to prevent the act.
COUNT 10 | THE TARGET. The person you were sent to stop is your older self. They are waiting at the end of the years the court has added.
addenda: ADDENDUM | Returned from {year}. The Bailiff reports another death. The court adds the years.
ADDENDUM | The record shows you reached farther this time. Your sentence increases regardless.
ADDENDUM | No new charge. The Tribunal remains in session. Your return has been entered into the record.
ADDENDUM | A juror asked whether these returns are changing who you are. The question was removed. The added years remain.
victory: The final note holds. The Idiot God closes its eyes. Time stops in a small space around it, and for the first time the dancers play quietly.
Far away, the clock on Mount Meridian moves. 21:14 becomes 21:15. The city has a tomorrow again.
You understand why your older self stopped time. The Long Door had let the god through. Holding the whole world still was the only way they knew to keep it from waking.
Your song can hold it here without stopping everyone else. But someone must keep playing. You sit beside the sleeping god, set the trumpet to your lips, and begin again.
The world moves on. You do not. Somewhere, a younger version of you will never need to build the Long Door.
The game is beaten. Boss rush is now available in the Holding. Clemency from this run has been added to your record.

bailiff.name: THE INTERDICTOR
bailiff.title: A machine waiting at the city limits. It carries the Tribunal's seal, an unsigned order, and one instruction: keep you from reaching 2081.

witness.name: THE WITNESS
witness.title: It has watched the ice for longer than anyone remembers. It has seen your future, but something keeps it from speaking.

defendant.name: THE DEFENDANT
defendant.title: Your older self. They know what happens after the clocks stop. They are prepared to do it again.

executor.name: THE EXECUTOR
executor.title: A machine sent to end your research. Its orders are sealed inside its turret.

chief.name: THE SECTION CHIEF
chief.title: He has orders to clear the house. Your scientists are first on his list.

azathoth.name: THE IDIOT GOD
azathoth.title: Something from outside time. It hears the Long Door opening. Its dancers keep it awake.

pioneer.name: THE PIONEER
pioneer.title: The expedition lost its pilot. The walking frame carried on without one.

blaster.name: THE BLASTER
blaster.title: Sent ahead of the Executor to clear its way into the house.

chumbles.name: CHUMBLES
chumbles.title: It is breakfast. He has not been fed to his satisfaction.

gallows_oak.name: THE GALLOWS OAK
gallows_oak.title: It was old when the city was a ford. The Long Door's frame was cut from it.

summons.name: THE SUMMONS
summons.title: A summons compels you to appear. This one comes up out of the lake.

waiting_city.title: THE YEARS BETWEEN
lines: The Interdictor falls beneath the stopped clock at the Court of Hours. Inside its chest is a transfer warrant. Your destination was changed from 2081 to 2031. The authorization line is blank.
The Bailiff brought you where the warrant told it to. The Interdictor was waiting to make sure you never reached the Observatory. Someone changed your route before the journey began.

The machine is destroyed. The Bailiff still returns you to the Tribunal when you die. For now, the road out of the city is clear. You use what you know of the next fifty years to build a fortune. By 2044 you run one of Meridian's largest firms.
You need a key to enter the Observatory. The last known key belonged to Ines Calder, its first keeper. She took it north aboard the Long Patience in 2039. The ship never returned.
You know where the key will be found. You also know who is supposed to find it. You intend to reach it first.
Spring, 2046. You fund an expedition into the White Waste. Meridian is thirty-five years from the Stilling. You have a ship, a crew, and one lead.

white_waste.title: WHAT THE WITNESS SAW
lines: As the Witness falls, the ice around it clears. Inside is a woman in a red coat, asleep. Ines Calder. The Observatory key hangs at her neck. You take it. She does not wake.
The Witness speaks. It says it has seen what you will do with the key. Something so terrible that time itself will stop.
You ask what happens. Its mouth opens, but the answer never comes. The Witness falls silent before it can tell you why.
You return to Meridian with the key sealed away. In 2047, you buy a house on Calder Hill and turn it into a research estate. You have ten years to prevent the future you have been shown.
You hire scientists and engineers. They test every theory you can afford. Nothing explains how to stop time from breaking. You spend the fortune you made trying.
Autumn, 2056. Armed men in grey arrive during a storm. Every one of them has the same face. They kill your staff and enter the house. You are still inside.

glass_house.title: THE ORDERS
lines: The Executor stops moving in the ruined conservatory. Rain falls through the broken glass. The house is quiet.

You find its orders in a steel case. They were typed on the machine in your own safe room. In the corner is the same seal as the Interdictor's warrant. The date is March 14, 2081. The signature is yours.
Raid Calder Hill. Destroy the research. Kill the scientists if necessary. Below that, in your handwriting: Time must break. If it does not, everything else will.
Your older self ordered the raid. The matching seal links these orders to the warrant that stranded you in 2031. They have been trying to keep you from the Observatory since the beginning.
You have considered dying to end the cycle. The court will not permit it. Each time you fall, it returns you to the past and adds more years.
March 14, 2081. You climb Mount Meridian toward the Observatory and the Long Door. The clock reads 21:14. Figures in your coat wait along the path. You taught them how to fight.

the_ascent.title: THE DOOR
lines: Your older self falls beside the Long Door. They look at you and say, quietly: I would do it again.
The sky opens. Something enormous moves through the gap. It has no shape that can remain still. The stone beneath you begins to give way.
The Long Door was never an ordinary clock. You built it to preserve one evening for one person. But the opening reached outside time. The god heard it and came toward your world.

Your older self stopped Meridian at 21:14 to keep that opening from widening. The Tribunal saw nine million people trapped in one evening. It called the Stilling the crime. It never understood what the Stilling was holding back.
So the Tribunal took another version of you from another timeline and told you to stop the Defendant. You did what it ordered. Now the lock is broken. The original mistake was opening the Long Door.
The god pulls you inside. Space turns back on itself. In your pack is the worn trumpet you found at the Hermitage, the one your older self carried. You brought it without knowing why.

brief.title: THE LAST SENTENCE
lines: On Mount Meridian, the clock advances from 21:14 to 21:15. The Tribunal notices. No one has authorized time to move.
The Defendant still waits at the Observatory. Beyond the Long Door, a trumpet is keeping something asleep. The court knows only that its original sentence has failed.
It reaches into another timeline and takes another you. You have never heard the lullaby. The court tells you what it told the first: return to 2031 and stop yourself.

This time there are no breaks between the years. Cross the Waiting City, the White Waste, the Glass House, and the Ascent in one run. Every fight is harder. You cannot return to the Holding until the mission ends.
Rain strikes the crater. The year is 2031. You begin again.

waiting_city.title: THE YEARS AGAIN
lines: The Interdictor falls beneath the stopped clock. Inside is the same altered transfer warrant: 2031, no authorization. The court file said you would find it. Someone has lived these years before.
You follow the same years: the company, the fortune, the Observatory key lost to the ice. In spring 2046, you sail north.

white_waste.title: THE KEY AGAIN
lines: The Witness looks at you and tries to speak. This time it says nothing. It turns toward Mount Meridian, as though listening.
You take Ines Calder's key, return to Meridian, and build your laboratories. In 2056 the grey men arrive, just as the record said.

glass_house.title: THE ORDERS AGAIN
lines: You defeat the Executor. Its orders are still signed by your future self. Nothing in the record has changed.
At the Observatory, on March 14, 2081, the clock is fixed at 21:14. Your older self waits inside the ring of stones.

the_ascent.title: REALITY BREAKS
lines: The Defendant falls. Once again, they say: I would do it again. Then they look toward the sky, waiting for something that does not come.
The god is already asleep. Somewhere outside time, the first of you is still playing the trumpet. There is no god left to come through the door.
The Tribunal has ordered an event that can no longer happen. It sent you to prevent a future another version of you has already changed. Both outcomes occupy the same moment.
The mountain breaks apart. Stone and sky fall away. Through the white light you hear a familiar, impatient voice.
You wake in your own bed on a Saturday morning. Chumbles is sitting on your chest. He sees your eyes open, hops down, and heads for the kitchen.

victory: Chumbles sits on the kitchen floor, back to his usual size. He watches you as though nothing unusual has happened.
You open the cupboard, find his treats, and give him some. He eats them, then checks the floor for more.
He settles on the sunny end of the sofa and goes to sleep. Somewhere, a trumpet is still playing. Somewhere, a clock reads 21:15. This morning, you are home.
The last sentence is served. Clemency from this run has been added to your record.

interlude.title: DOWNRIVER
lines: The Executor stops moving in the ruined conservatory. Its orders are in a steel case, signed by you, dated March 14, 2081.
Under the signature is a requisition you have not written yet: one frame, Gallows Oak, cut at Lake Stillwater. The Long Door will be built from it.
If the tree burns, there is no frame. If there is no frame, there is no Door.
Ten years go by in the empty house. In 2066 you go down to the river below Calder Hill, past the old weir, toward the lake.
The water is fast and cold. Nothing that falls in comes out where it went in.

victory: The Summons comes apart over the lake. The crown of the Gallows Oak catches, and the fire runs down the trunk to the water.
By morning the Oak is black to the waterline. There will be no frame for the Long Door from this tree.
Across the lake, on the far shore, something has noticed the smoke.
This build ends here. The far shore is sealed for now.
